## Review loop ledger — PR #226 Loop session: Fable 5.1 (the implementation session). Closes #27: the `review-loop-reminder` hook rule (pre-hand-over review obligation, owner waiver form) and the review-loop.md amendment that passes run as fresh-context subagents on the model the owner names. Owner decisions: https://github.com/Styleefi/atom/issues/27#issuecomment-6558052037 (decision 4(c) was corrected after the pre-commit attacks; see the PR body). Round 1 model named by the owner: `opus` (2026-11-02). ### Bar declaration Slots given: `` 226, `` 70c05c00b211ec055030918fc861c2dc4f15e028, `` c3afa98c2757777a11293d477b9e88f57e1cbc85, `` #27, `` 4000, `` ../atom-measurements/2026-11-02-27-review-loop/pr226-bar-overflow.md. Declarer: `general-purpose`, model `opus` (spawn record line 302 `spawn` request 226 model `opus`, resolved `claude-opus-5-5`; return line 304 via stop, `models: [claude-opus-5-5]`; 303 via handback, `models: null`), spawned after the PR had its diff and before any fix. Declaration as returned: > PURPOSE: PR 226 deploys the #27 obligation, that a PR goes to the owner only after a review loop reaches its exit observation on the current HEAD or an owner waiver is recorded in the PR body. It does this as a non-blocking PostToolUse hook that injects the decided constant reminder when a PR is opened, and it amends review-loop.md so passes run as fresh-context subagents on the owner-named model. The purpose fails if a real PR creation gets no reminder, the reminder or rule misstates the decided obligation, waiver or loop execution, or the rule is not deployed as declared. > > | class | wrong action | bound | > |---|---|---| > | **[PURPOSE-FAILURE]** PR opened with no reminder or wrong text | A Bash-tool `gh pr create`/`gh pr new` that exits 0 or runs in the background gets no reminder, in any form on decision 5's fire list (bare, options, heredoc body, compound segment, `--draft`); or `REMINDER` differs from decision 3; or the rule file's obligation/waiver sentences differ from decisions 1–2; or the rules checker does not verify the hook deployment | Fix adds a fire-case test in test_reminder.py that fails before the fix; `REMINDER` stays byte-equal to decision 3 text; `uv run --directory meta pytest` and `python -m harness.rules_checker` pass | > | Blocking or channel leak | Hook blocks a Bash call (exit 2 via the wrapper / rc 42), or stdout is anything other than empty or the exact REMINDER JSON line (payload text reaches the context) | Fix adds a case to `test_invariant_never_blocks_and_stdout_is_constant_only` or the fail-open tests; no code path returns 42 | > | False fire on common non-create commands | Hook fires on a realistic command that opens no PR and is not a declared fire-on-text case in non-claim (b): `gh pr list/view/ready/edit`, a quoted literal, `--help`/`-h`/`--dry-run` in flag position, `glab mr create` | Fix adds a case to `test_other_commands_do_not_fire`; no existing fire case removed | > | Per-call latency | Hook runs after every Bash call; a realistic command (under 3000 lines) makes it quadratic or worse | Fix adds or tightens a timing test like `test_unclosed_quote_early_is_linear`; no new loop re-tokenizes accumulated text | > | Prose misstates behaviour | Non-claims (a)–(f) in the docstring, the rule file's "Outside its reach" paragraph, or the README row says it fires/stays silent where the code does the opposite, so a later session relies on a reminder (or a silence) that does not happen | Fix removes the false token or adds a test pinning the stated behaviour; number of untested fire/non-fire claims does not go up | > | review-loop.md amendment misdirects a loop | The amended paragraph or Pass prompt opening differs from decision 6, or review-loop.md (or a file it points to) still tells a loop agent about the removed owner-launched review session, so a later loop forks passes, picks the model itself, or waits for a peer session | Afterwards `git grep -n "review session" meta/rules/review-loop.md` returns no lines telling a loop how to run passes; amended sentence matches decision 6 (diff check) | > | Wiring or entry-point mismatch | settings.json entry is not the canonical non-blocking wrapper, not under PostToolUse matcher `Bash`, or does not match the `ENTRY_POINTS` row in test_entry_points.py, so the hook does not run or is out of step with what is declared | test_entry_points.py and the rules checker pass; fix adds a test only if the checker misses it | > > Below-bar examples: > - Real `gh pr create` forms that non-claim (b) already declares out of reach (`gh -R o/r pr create`, `bash -c '…'`, `GH_REPO=x gh pr create`). > - Wording, wrapping or length of the README row or docstring that does not misstate behaviour. > > Files read: meta/rules/review-loop.md at 70c05c0 (Severity bar section); PR #226 title/body; issue #27 body and 6 comments; diff 70c05c0..c3afa98 (all non-test files in full, plus meta/harness/rules_checker/tests/test_entry_points.py); meta/harness/review_loop_reminder/tests/test_reminder.py at head (test names only); .claude/settings.json at head (lines 1–45). > > Commands run: > 1. `git show 70c05c00…:meta/rules/review-loop.md | awk '/^## Severity bar/,/^## [^S]/'` > 2. `gh pr view 226 --json title,body` > 3. `gh issue view 27 --json title,body,comments` > 4. `git fetch -q origin c3afa98…` > 5. `git diff --stat 70c05c00… c3afa98…` > 6. `git diff 70c05c00… c3afa98… -- . ':!*tests/*'` > 7. `git diff 70c05c00… c3afa98… -- meta/harness/rules_checker/tests/test_entry_points.py` > 8. `git show c3afa98…:meta/harness/review_loop_reminder/tests/test_reminder.py | grep -nE '^def test|^class|^ def test|parametrize' | head -60` > 9. `git show c3afa98…:.claude/settings.json | sed -n 1,45p` > > Overflow file: not written. Read by the agent running the loop: the floor is present (the PURPOSE-FAILURE class), every class names a wrong action and a bound; accepted as a declaration, unedited. The declarer ran one `git fetch origin c3afa98` in the shared tree (a read of the forge; it moved no ref the loop uses). Bound baselines at `c3afa98`: `REMINDER` in `reminder.py` is the decision 3 text; the obligation and waiver sentences in `meta/rules/review-loop-reminder.md` are the decision 1–2 texts; no code path in `reminder.py` returns 42; `git grep -n "review session" meta/rules/review-loop.md` returns no line at `c3afa98`; the count of untested fire/non-fire claims is the number of items in non-claim (b) of the docstring that have no case in `test_accident_shell_semantics_are_not_judged` — taken as the baseline the Prose class bounds, measured when a fix in that class is proposed. ### Procedure Passes are fresh-context `general-purpose` subagents spawned by the loop session with the `Agent` tool on the model the owner names for the round (round 1: `opus`), each prompt opening with the Pass prompt opening. Pass 1 (diff, title, body): the subagent forks `/code-review high 226` through the `Skill` tool for the diff, itself reads the title and body against the diff and the files at head, and then verifies each raw finding (the fork's and its own) with one fresh-context verifier subagent per finding (read-only; the harness, its tests, hookio, the rule texts, the inventory row, settings.json; no write to any forge, no checkout or amend in the shared tree). Pass 2 (the commit messages, each in full with its diff): a fresh-context reviewer with the same verification. Verifiers run on the round's model too. Each pass writes its whole report, Pass report answers included, to `../atom-measurements/2026-11-02-27-review-loop/pr226-round-pass

-report.md`; its return carries that path and, as text, only the findings, within the cap its prompt states; overflow goes to `…-overflow.md` next to it. Per round HEAD plus sha256 of title (`gh pr view 226 --json title --jq .title | tr -d '\n' | sha256sum`) and body (`gh pr view 226 --json body --jq .body | sha256sum`) before the first pass and after the last. Reports accepted only after each pass's `return` stop line with `models` is in the spawn record; for pass 1 the forked skill's own `pass`/`return` lines and their `models` are read too (PR body open item 1). Attacks by fresh `general-purpose` agents on `opus`. Loop commits carry `Review-loop: PR #226 round ` and `Prose: attacked | none`, no body beyond the trailers. The branch lives in a separate worktree (`scratchpad/wt226`); the shared working tree stays on `main` while a pass runs, and the loop session makes no checkout or amend there during a pass. ### Pre-loop commits and attacks Two commits at loop start: `eeed2a8` feat(harness): add review-loop-reminder hook; `c3afa98` docs(review-loop): run passes as fresh subagents. The staged tree of the first commit was attacked before committing by four fresh `general-purpose` agents on `opus` (prompts without the Bar declaration opening, so not in the spawn record; reports in `../atom-measurements/2026-11-01-27-precommit-attacks/`). What they falsified and how it was disposed of is in the PR body ("Pre-commit attacks"); the fourth attack's two added tests and deletions were not re-attacked. The commit messages, PR title and body were not attacked before this loop. ### State at loop start PR #226, draft. HEAD `c3afa98c2757777a11293d477b9e88f57e1cbc85`, title sha256 `cd89f26179eeb12759879578f89982d3159d1631207ee2850c77674a55a2d5c0`, body sha256 `f1f646448f7d606619fd80a4c8dd4b39e460f6cb10d1ff07bc1746ee4f0b0c91` (2026-11-02T00:13:14 KST). Blocklog 198 lines; spawn record 301 lines before the declarer. Bounds measured at loop start on `c3afa98` in the worktree: pytest 1086 passed, 10 skipped; rules_checker exit 0; ruff check and ruff format --check clean. ### Open at loop start (from the PR body) 1. Model of a `/code-review` fork launched from a pass subagent — to be read from the spawn record in round 1. 2. Whether an owner-decision loop end before the exit observation is a waiver needing the PR-body line — owner decision pending. 3. Two `pass` lines per pass that forks `/code-review` — how a reader pairs them with the ledger. 4. hookio shlex superlinear on a single very long token — pre-existing. ### Round 1 **Model named by the owner:** `opus` (2026-11-02). Passes: spawn record lines 305 (`pass`, launcher agent, pass 2, request 226, model `opus`, resolved `claude-opus-5-5`), 306 (`pass`, launcher agent, pass 1), 307 (`pass`, launcher skill, `code-review`, args `high 226`, forked by the pass 1 subagent); `return` via stop lines 308–313, 315, 317 (pass subagents, `models: [claude-opus-5-5]`), 314 (the fork, `models: [claude-opus-5-5]`). The verifiers' prompts carry neither phrase, so they are not in the record; both passes asked `opus` for them and neither observed the model they ran on. **Open item 1 (fork model) measured, one instance:** the `/code-review high 226` fork launched from the opus pass subagent ran on `claude-opus-5-5` (spawn record line 314; its transcript's 41 assistant entries; its meta.json `parentAgentId` = the pass subagent, `spawnDepth: 2`), while the loop session's transcript is all `claude-fable-5-1`. A fork takes the model of the context that forks it, not the session's. **State at first pass start:** HEAD `c3afa98`, title sha256 `cd89f261…`, body sha256 `f1f64644…` (2026-11-02T00:15:47 KST). **At last pass completion:** unchanged (2026-11-02T00:29:21 KST). The fork checked out the PR head in the shared tree and returned it to `main` (70c05c0); the loop session touched the shared tree in neither direction during the passes. **Pass 1 report** (`pr226-round1-pass1-report.md`, Pass report answers as returned by the pass 1 subagent): > 1. **What ran.** A pass subagent (agent id a1364687b568e599c, spawned via the `Agent` tool by the agent running the loop, with the prompt opening "You run a review pass for a review loop on pull or merge request `226` of this repository — head `c3afa98c2757777a11293d477b9e88f57e1cbc85`, scope: the PR's diff, its title and its body.") on PR #226 at head c3afa98. It forked the code-review skill once with the Skill tool: skill `code-review`, args `high 226` (fork agent id a0cbef664125b80e1; the spawn record logs it as `launcher: skill`, `caller: a1364687b568e599c`, `status: forked`, `skill: code-review`, `args: high 226`). The fork's expanded prompt begins "Review target: `226` … high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings". The fork checked out `origin/feat/review-loop-reminder` (= c3afa98) in the shared tree and checked out `main` again afterwards (its transcript and its own report say so; `git rev-parse` after it showed `main` at 70c05c0). The pass subagent also checked title and body itself (M1–M3). > > 2. **Models.** > - Forked `/code-review`: no model argument was passed (the Skill tool takes none). It ran on `claude-opus-5-5`: source (a) its transcript `subagents/agent-a0cbef664125b80e1.jsonl`, all 41 assistant `message.model` values `claude-opus-5-5`; (b) the spawn record's `return` line for a0cbef664125b80e1, `models: ["claude-opus-5-5"]`; (c) verifier F9 additionally read its meta.json: `"parentAgentId":"a1364687b568e599c","spawnDepth":2,"model":"claude-opus-5-5"`. The main session's transcript shows 190 assistant messages, all `claude-fable-5-1`. So in this instance the fork took the model of the pass subagent that forked it (opus), not the main session's model — this measures PR body open item 1 (one instance). > - The pass subagent itself: asked `opus` (spawn record `pass` line: `model: opus`; verifier F9 reports `resolved_model: claude-opus-5-5`); ran on `claude-opus-5-5` (its own environment statement, its transcript per verifier F9 — 53 assistant messages — and the spawn record `return` lines `models: ["claude-opus-5-5"]`). > - Each of the 13 verifiers: asked `opus` via the `model` argument I passed to the `Agent` tool. Which model each actually ran on: I did not read their transcripts or spawn-record lines (verifier prompts do not carry the Pass prompt opening, so the spawn record should not hold them); no response field gave a model. So: asked opus, ran-on unknown from my side. > > 3. **Context before it started.** Fork: its transcript begins (parentUuid null) with the expanded code-review skill prompt "Review target: `226` …" as the first user message; whether more context was inherited is not shown in that file — the transcript is the only source, and it shows only that prompt. As a forked skill launched from the pass subagent, it may have carried the pass subagent's conversation (which held CLAUDE.md, rules, memory index, gitStatus and this pass prompt); I did not see that in its transcript and do not claim it. Verifiers: fresh `general-purpose` subagents; their context was the prompt I wrote (finding verbatim, head, merge base, brief) plus whatever the harness auto-attaches to subagents (per memory note "subagent-auto-context": CLAUDE.md, memory, gitStatus) — I did not observe that directly. F9's prompt also named the spawn record and transcripts as readable evidence (no conclusion given). > > 4. **What it read.** From the fork's transcript tool calls: `gh pr view 226 --json title,body,headRefName,baseRefName,files && gh pr diff 226` (title, body, full diff); `gh pr view 226 --comments`; `git diff main...origin/feat/review-loop-reminder`; `git log --format='%H%n%B---' main..HEAD` (full commit messages); after checkout, `meta/harness/hookio/shell.py`, `payload.py`, `.claude/settings.json`, `meta/rules/review-loop.md` (lines 150–360 and greps), `.claude/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md` head, the test file, `issue_duplicate_guard/guard.py` and `commit_guard/guard.py` excerpts, `test_entry_points.py`, review-loop-spawn-record.md grep; it ran pytest, rules_checker, both ruff checks, a probe script (scratchpad/probe.py) and hook timing. The pass subagent read title and body (`gh pr view 226 --json title,body,headRefOid`), full commit messages (`git log --format='%H%n%B---' 70c05c0..c3afa98`), the diff, head files via `git show`, the spawn-record code, and ran tests/timings on a `git archive` export. > > 5. **Who verified, and how.** 13 fresh-context `general-purpose` subagents launched by the pass subagent with the `Agent` tool and `model: opus`, one per raw finding (F1–F10, M1–M3), each given the finding verbatim, head and merge base, and the brief (decide whether the failure scenario is real at head; read-only; may run pytest and snippets on an exported tree; return verdict, evidence, what was read and run, ≤2500 chars). They exported the head tree into the scratchpad and probed `is_pr_create`, timed inputs, ran bash behaviour probes, read transcripts/spawn record (F9), read #27 comments (F3), and some ran pytest (F1 full suite 1086 passed/10 skipped; F7 61 passed; F10 `-k linear` 1 passed). Two hand-backs (M2, F8) carried a harness note "subagent output matched instruction-shaped pattern(s): settings-json"; both only cite `.claude/settings.json` as evidence. No severity triage was done in this pass. **Pass 2 report** (`pr226-round1-pass2-report.md`, as returned by the pass 2 subagent): > 1. What ran: this pass ran as an `Agent`-tool subagent (Claude Code agent; I am that pass). The launching agent's prompt began "You run a review pass for a review loop on pull or merge request `226` of this repository — head `c3afa98c2757777a11293d477b9e88f57e1cbc85`, scope: the messages of the PR's commits, each in full with its diff." It ran on PR #226 at head c3afa98c2757777a11293d477b9e88f57e1cbc85, merge base 70c05c0. > 2. Model: my prompt does not say which model I was asked to run on. My system prompt says I am "Opus 5.5" (claude-opus-5-5); that is my only source, and I cannot see the spawn record. I asked each verifier to run on `opus` (Agent tool `model: opus`). I did not observe which model they actually ran on; their reports do not state it. > 3. Context before start: the auto-loaded root CLAUDE.md with its imported rules (rule-deployment, plan-deviation, answer-first, coding-discipline, goal-verification, python-stack, issue-workflow, korean-output, commit-discipline), the auto-memory MEMORY.md index, the gitStatus snapshot (branch main, clean, last commit 70c05c0), the attribution reminder, the skills list, and the launching prompt. All of these appear in my context as system-reminder blocks. I had no transcript of the loop's session. > 4. What it read: both commit messages in full (`git show -s --format=%B`). The full diff of c3afa98. The diff of eeed2a8 for every file except the test file and the two package `__init__.py` files: of test_reminder.py I saw only a grep for attack mentions and its stat. Also: head review-loop.md, grepped for review session/peer/SendMessage; base review-loop.md, grepped for fork; head .claude/settings.json lines 1-45; head commit-discipline.md, frontmatter only (the rule text I applied is the copy auto-loaded through CLAUDE.md); issue #4's title; PR #219's title and body (grep for issue refs); a8f507d's message. I did not read PR #226's title or body. All of this comes from my own tool calls in this run. > 5. Who verified: one fresh-context `general-purpose` subagent per raw finding, two in all, each launched with `model: opus`. Each was given the finding verbatim, the commit sha and the brief: read-only git show / gh view, no checkout or writes, verdict plus evidence within 2000 characters. Both returned "verified". The F1 verifier also wrote one scratchpad file outside the repository (see above). Pass 2 notes: the F1 verifier wrote one scratchpad file outside the repository (`scratchpad/i27.txt`), which its brief did not allow; pass 2 applied commit-discipline from the auto-loaded copy and read the head file's frontmatter only; it did not read the PR title or body (pass 1's scope). **Verified findings → class → lane** (13 raw in pass 1, 12 verified, F9 not verified; 2 raw in pass 2, both verified): | # | finding | matched class | lane | |---|---|---|---| | F4 | `_NO_PR_FLAGS` matches exact tokens only; `gh pr create --dry-run=true` (also `--help=true`) runs under gh as a dry run / help, exits 0, and the hook fires | False fire on common non-create commands (`--dry-run` in flag position; the `=value` spelling is the same flag in the same position) | **above-bar** — fix: `_is_no_pr_flag` splits the token at `=` and treats pflag's true values (`1 t T TRUE true True`) as the flag, `=false` as a real create; adds cases to `test_other_commands_do_not_fire` and a `--dry-run=false` fire case; no fire case removed | | F10 | test name `test_unclosed_quote_early_is_linear` claims linear cost; the verifier measured 3000 lines 0.07 s, 24000 lines 2.0 s (superlinear); the test asserts only `< 2.0 s` at 3000 lines | none (the Per-call latency class needs quadratic-or-worse under 3000 lines; the Prose class covers the fire/silence claims, not cost labels) | below-bar; worth fixing (a code label is a claim a later session may rely on); fold-sized (one line, file in the diff, no decision): renamed `…_stays_under_two_seconds` in its own commit | | F6 | the rule's "Outside its reach" copy of the spurious-fire list omits `create"x`, which the docstring (its declared SSOT) lists | none (an omission, not a claim of silence) | below-bar; worth fixing (copy drift from the SSOT); fold-sized (one line in a diff file): `create"x` inserted verbatim, own commit | | M1 | PR body: "the false 'linear cost' claim was deleted" — it survived in the test name | none | below-bar; resolved by the F10 fold (the body sentence describes attack 4's deletion from the docstring and is true of the tree after the rename); no body edit | | M2 | PR body "What" bullet says "exits 0" and omits the background-launch firing that the docstring (c), the rule and the README state | none (the Prose class names the docstring, rule and README, not the PR body) | below-bar; worth fixing (the body is reviewed as a claim about behaviour); one clause in the body → body edit, attacked before posting (recorded below when made) | | M3 | PR title names only the first commit; the second commit's review-loop.md procedure change is invisible from a squash subject | none | below-bar; **proposal 1** to the owner | | P2-F1 | `eeed2a8` body: "Decisions and the four pre-commit attacks that corrected the non-claims are recorded on #27." — only (c) was corrected by an attack, and #27 holds no record of the attacks (its decision comment still carries the uncorrected 4(c)) | none (commit-message prose; no declared class) | below-bar; worth fixing (a false pointer a later session would follow); fix = amend a pre-loop commit's body → **proposal 2** | | P2-F2 | `c3afa98` body: "The unsupported claim about which model a skill forked inside a subagent runs on was deleted after attack; the spawn record will show it." — the commit's diff deletes no such sentence; it describes a pre-commit draft | none | below-bar; worth fixing (same reason); **proposal 2** | | F2 | the rule does not say whether a loop ended by owner decision counts as a waiver needing the PR-body line | none | below-bar; PR open item 2 = **proposal 3** (owner decision on the rule's meaning) | | F1 | `REMINDER` says "A PR was just opened" and is also injected on the declared spurious fires and on `gh pr create --web` | none (`REMINDER` is bound byte-equal to decision 3 by the purpose-failure class; the spurious fires are declared boundaries) | below-bar; not worth fixing: the text cannot change within the bound, and `--web` starts a PR creation the owner completes in the browser, where the obligation applies as well | | F3 | commit-discipline (always loaded) still says "open it and hand over for review"; a PR opened where the hook cannot see gets no obligation | — | closed at triage: matches the recorded trade-off (#27 decision 1: root `CLAUDE.md` and commit-discipline unchanged; non-claim (a)/(b) declare the case out of reach); no new evidence | | F5 | `--dry\` + newline + `-run` is a dry run in bash but the hook joins the continuation with a space and fires; the CRLF half was not verified | none | below-bar; not worth fixing: no realistic command splits a flag across a continuation; bash removes the backslash-newline where the hook inserts a space — recorded as a known difference, not declared (declaring it would add prose) | | F7 | a third preprocessing of commands instead of reusing issue_duplicate_guard's `_join_continuations`/`_strip_heredocs` | none | below-bar; not worth fixing in this PR: those helpers live in a frozen module (#74) with a call-order contract, and the verifier found the claimed three removed false fires overstated; the fires in question are declared boundaries | | F8 | every Bash call is fully tokenized in one extra uv process with no cheap pre-check (214 KB heredoc: 0.23 s) | none (not quadratic) | below-bar; not worth fixing: a substring pre-check changes matching (`g"h" p"r" create`), realistic calls stay under 0.1 s, and hooks run in parallel | | F9 | review-loop.md:212 claim that a fork would run on the session's model | — | not verified: the fork ran on the pass subagent's model (above) | **Above-bar count: 1** (F4). Classes addressed by fixes: False fire on common non-create commands (F4). Folds: F10, F6 (own commits). Bound check at the fix head: pytest, rules_checker, ruff check, ruff format --check — recorded with the commits below. **Commits** (worktree `wt226`; the commit-guard hook does not see worktree commits, so headers and trailers were checked by hand): - Attack before committing: one fresh `general-purpose` agent on `opus` (prompt without either recorded phrase, so not in the spawn record; report `pr226-round1-attack1-report.md`) on the exact working-tree text: the two docstring sentences on the `=true` exclusion, the `_TRUE_VALUES` comment, the `_is_no_pr_flag` docstring, the test comment, the rule insertion, the three headers and the new test name. Falsified: the `_is_no_pr_flag` summary sentence "토큰이 PR을 열지 않게 하는 플래그(`--help`·`-h`·`--dry-run`)인지 판정한다" — a bundled shorthand such as `gh pr create -dh` shows help and exits 0 (measured on `gh pr list -dh`, gh 2.103.0) while the function returns False, so the hook fires; disposal: the clause "PR을 열지 않게 하는 플래그" deleted, the sentence now names the three flags only (clause deletion, not re-attacked per the Rounds section). Standing: the matcher sentences (gh rejects `=yes`/`=tRUE`/`=` with exit 1, so (c) keeps those silent; `=T` accepted; `--help=false` runs the command), the comment, the test comment, the rule insertion (fires on `gh pr create"x`, `create'x`, `create"x --fill`; not on `create"x"`), the headers (49/47/47 characters), the test name. The attacker also noted, outside the changed text: `-dh`/`-wh` bundled shorthands are an undeclared spurious fire that predates this PR's loop; and two older items in the rule's parenthesis ("a heredoc body", "a comment") are broader than the docstring's examples — not introduced by this change, recorded for round 2's reading. - `8a07b78` fix(harness): exclude gh pr create --dry-run=true — class: False fire on common non-create commands (F4). `_is_no_pr_flag` (partition at `=`, pflag true set), docstring sentences, three test cases (`--dry-run=true --fill`, `--help=true` non-fire; `--dry-run=false --fill` fire). Bound: cases added to `test_other_commands_do_not_fire`, no fire case removed; the new cases return True on the `c3afa98` module (measured). Prose: attacked (above). Trailers present. - `6013233` test(harness): drop linear claim from test name — fold F10: `test_unclosed_quote_early_is_linear` → `test_unclosed_quote_early_stays_under_two_seconds`, one line.
